newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch police find alleged UK child sex abuse tape.
newsitem.headline: Dutch police find alleged UK child sex abuse tape.

text.p: Dutch police said on Friday a house search in Amsterdam had uncovered the master-tape of a child pornography video allegedly made by a British paedophile ring operating in the Netherlands in the early 1990s.
Police searching the house of a 46-year-old Dutchman charged with sexually abusing under-age Thai boys discovered the "Bjorn Tape" in a basement cupboard, spokesman Klaas Wilting said.

Thought to have been made in 1990, the Bjorn Tape featured prominently in recent British media reports alleging a British-led porn ring in Amsterdam made and distributed at least five so-called "snuff" porn movies in which teenage and pre-teen boys were sexually abused to death.
The house owner, identified only as B. de L, said he had been given the tape by an unnamed Englishman in return for a 1,000 guilder loan, Wilting said.
"We are investigating his statement," Wilting said, but declined to comment whether the Briton had been interviewed.
Wilting said the blood-smeared and apparently lifeless boy featured in the film had since been traced by police and was found to be "physically well".
Contrary to earlier reports which alleged the boy was one of a number of homeless pre-teens abducted by the gang from Britain and Eastern Europe, "Bjorn" was Dutch, Wilting said.
Dutch police said in April a renewed probe into allegations of child sex murders raised by a British television documentary earlier this year had yielded no fresh evidence.
The documentary, "The Boy Business", claimed homeless boys were kidnapped and subjected to sexual torture on film by the Amsterdam-based gang, which later dumped their bodies on the city's outskirts.
Wilting said B. de L. was being held on charges of abusing two boys aged eight and 10 during a visit to Pattaya, Thailand. He has also been charged with drug possession.
He will be prosecuted in Amsterdam but no trial date has yet been set, he said.
Wilting said a Dutch investigative team had travelled to Thailand in late December, where they interviewed a man in Pattaya who had allgedely procured boys for B. de L. for money.
Video recordings of the alleged abuse were found at B. de L.'s home, Wilting said.
